points.label: Action and response
points.left: Hezekiah removes high places and the bronze serpent, trusts the LORD, keeps commands, and is said to do right according to David.
points.right: Solomon kneels before the assembly and prays across sin, defeat, drought, exile, foreigners, war, and return before asking God to remember mercies to David.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places David functions as a remembered royal measure inside reform inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places Davidic promise is carried into a prayer broad enough to imagine exile and return inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 2 Kings 18:1–8 and 2 Chronicles 6:12–42 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Royal, Poetic, and Prophetic Memory” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Solomon’s Temple prayer repeatedly returns to David

payload.tension: 2 Kings 18:1–8 foregrounds David functions as a remembered royal measure inside reform; 2 Chronicles 6:12–42 foregrounds Davidic promise is carried into a prayer broad enough to imagine exile and return. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
